decision.coverage_assessment: Partial. Multiple westnile.ca.gov weekly update PDFs are present with 2024 cumulative case counts (98–112 human cases from 23+ counties), and the LA County WNV data page was found. However, no snippet confirms August-specific case counts, deaths, or hospitalizations within the 2024-08-01 to 2024-08-31 window. The CDC ArboNET historic data page was found but covers 1999–2025 aggregates, not 2024 provisional monthly data. The westnile.ca.gov homepage shows 2026 data (current year), confirming the site is live but the August 2024 weekly reports need date-specific identification. Facebook and beaconbio.org results are low-value for this task.
decision.source_diversity_assessment: Moderate. Source types present: official state agency (westnile.ca.gov, 9 results), federal agency (cdc.gov, 4 results), county health (publichealth.lacounty.gov, 1 result), news (latimes.com, abcnews.com, today.com, cidrap.umn.edu, 4 results), social media (facebook.com, 3 results — low value), academic (pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov, jamanetwork.com — not August 2024 specific), vector control (glamosquito.org, lawestvector.org — potentially useful for locality data). decision.trustworthiness_assessment: High for westnile.ca.gov (official CDPH-affiliated state surveillance site) and cdc.gov. Moderate for publichealth.lacounty.gov (official county source but snippet is general, not August 2024 specific). Low for facebook.com and beaconbio.org. The PMC article covers 2013–2024 aggregate mortality data, not August 2024 California-specific. News sources (latimes.com, cidrap.umn.edu) may contain August 2024 quotes citing official figures — worth pursuing if they appeared in the accepted candidates but were not in the top 10 summaries.
decision.disease_location_time_fit_assessment: Disease fit: Excellent — all top results are WNV-specific for California. Location fit: Good — California statewide and LA County covered; Sacramento, Kern, Fresno county-level sources not yet confirmed. Time fit: Weak — snippets reference 2024 cumulative figures but no snippet is anchored to August 2024 specifically. The weekly update PDFs (download_ids 4980, 5061, 5072) likely span different weeks of 2024 but their exact report dates are unknown from metadata alone. The gap between "98 cases" and "112 cases" across two PDFs suggests sequential weekly reports, but which weeks cover August is unconfirmed.
decision.corroboration_potential_assessment: Good potential. The westnile.ca.gov weekly PDFs are the primary source; CDC ArboNET 2024 provisional data can corroborate statewide totals; county health departments can corroborate locality-level data. The CIDRAP result (cidrap.umn.edu) is a credible secondary source that often cites official figures with evidence quotes. Iteration 2 should surface the westnile.ca.gov weekly report archive/index page to identify which download IDs correspond to August 2024 reports, and target the CDC 2024 WNV data page directly.

top_result_summaries.snippet: # West Nile virus in the United States. The West Nile virus quickly spread across the United States after the first reported cases in Queens, New York, in 1999. The reported number of infected in 2009 was 720, but the estimated total number of infected the same year was 54,000. In the first ten years since the virus arrived in the U.S., over 1,100 deaths occurred with human cases reported from every U.S. state except Maine, Alaska and Hawaii. Coverage is partially sufficient for the August 2024 window. The following target fields have candidate sources:

• deaths: fresnocountyca.gov press release cites CDPH reporting 4 deaths in 2024 as of 09-13-2024; the Facebook/CDPH snippet references "first human West Nile virus deaths" (undated, low trust).
• subnational_location / locality: Fresno County confirmed via fresnocountyca.gov and consolidatedmadca.gov; LA County via publichealth.lacounty.gov; Tulare County mentioned in westnile.ca.gov snippet; 23 counties referenced in the 98-case weekly update.
• date_reported: The Fresno County press release is dated 09-13-2024 (just outside the August window but citing cumulative 2024 figures); the consolidatedmadca.gov release is dated 07-10-2024 (just before the window). The westnile.ca.gov weekly PDFs lack confirmed publication dates in metadata.
• source_url / source_type / evidence_quote: Multiple candidate URLs with snippet-level evidence quotes available.

Remaining gaps:
• August-specific (2024-08-01 to 2024-08-31) weekly breakdowns: The westnile.ca.gov weekly PDFs have unknown publication dates from metadata alone — date anchoring requires page fetch, which is outside this workflow's scope.

Source diversity is adequate across tiers:
• State official: westnile.ca.gov (CDPH-operated, 9+2 results across iterations) — primary authoritative tier
• County official: fresnocountyca.gov, consolidatedmadca.gov (Fresno), publichealth.lacounty.gov (LA) — secondary official tier
• Federal official: cdc.gov (ArboNET historic data) — federal validation tier
• News/media: latimes.com, abc10.com, fresnobee.com, bakersfieldnow.com, abcnews.com, today.com — collection-support tier (cite official figures)
• Aggregator/surveillance: beaconbio.org — low priority, 2025-focused
• Low-trust: facebook.com (4 results) — not usable as primary evidence

Missing diversity: Sacramento County (saccounty.gov), Kern County (kernpublichealth.com), and Riverside County health departments did not surface as accepted candidates. CDPH press releases on cdph.ca.gov itself (distinct from westnile.ca.gov) did not appear as direct candidates.
decision.trustworthiness_assessment:
High trust: westnile.ca.gov (CDPH-operated state surveillance portal), fresnocountyca.gov (official county health department PDF press release with date 09-13-2024), consolidatedmadca.gov (official mosquito abatement district joint release with date 07-10-2024), publichealth.lacounty.gov (official LA County health), cdc.gov (federal ArboNET).

Medium trust: News outlets (abc10.com, fresnobee.com, bakersfieldnow.com, latimes.com) — acceptable as collection-support sources that cite official figures; evidence quotes must be traceable to named official sources.

Low trust / not usable as primary evidence: facebook.com posts (4 results) — social media reposts of CDPH content without direct URL to original CDPH press release; en.wikipedia.org — background only; ama-assn.org result is 2025-focused and not California-specific for August 2024; 19january2025snapshot.epa.gov — EPA technical documentation covering 2002–2023 national data, not California August 2024 specific.

Key trust caveat: The westnile.ca.gov weekly PDF download IDs (4980, 5061, 5072) have no confirmed publication dates in the metadata. The 112-case and 98-case cumulative figures cannot be definitively assigned to the August 2024 window without date confirmation. The fresnocountyca.gov press release (09-13-2024) citing 38 cases and 4 deaths is the most date-anchored official source, but it falls just outside the August 31 cutoff and reflects cumulative figures through early September.
decision.disease_location_time_fit_assessment:

Location fit: Good — primary candidates are California-specific (westnile.ca.gov, fresnocountyca.gov, publichealth.lacounty.gov, consolidatedmadca.gov). The CDC historic data page covers all U.S. states but includes California-filterable data. Some results (AMA 2025, BEACON 2025, Wikipedia, EPA technical doc) are national/multi-year and not California August 2024 specific — these are low-priority candidates.

Time fit: Partial — this is the most significant limitation. The task window is 2024-08-01 to 2024-08-31. The best-anchored official source (fresnocountyca.gov) is dated 09-13-2024 and reports cumulative figures through that date (38 cases, 4 deaths). The consolidatedmadca.gov release is dated 07-10-2024 (pre-window). The westnile.ca.gov weekly PDFs have unknown dates but their cumulative case counts (98 and 112) bracket a period that likely spans August 2024 based on the progression of the transmission season. No source has been confirmed to report August-specific (monthly) case counts — all figures are cumulative year-to-date, which is the standard CDPH reporting format. This is a structural limitation of the data source, not a search failure.
decision.corroboration_potential_assessment:
Strong corroboration potential exists between:
1. westnile.ca.gov weekly PDFs (primary state surveillance) and the fresnocountyca.gov press release (county-level, citing CDPH figures) — both reference CDPH as the authoritative data source, enabling cross-validation of cumulative 2024 case and death counts.
2. The CDC historic data page (cdc.gov) provides a federal-tier cross-check for annual California WNV totals, though it covers 1999–2025 aggregates rather than monthly breakdowns.
3. The consolidatedmadca.gov Fresno joint release (07-10-2024) corroborates early-season Fresno County case activity that feeds into the August cumulative figures.

Weaker corroboration: Facebook/social media snippets referencing CDPH press releases are low-trust and cannot be used as primary evidence without tracing to the original CDPH domain source. The AMA and BEACON results are 2025-focused and do not corroborate August 2024 California data.
